messages:
samir: FYI — customer (Acme Inc) filing: streaming responses from our hosted API are being truncated/partially delivered when the client sits behind a gRPC->HTTP1 gateway. They see a few SSE events, then connection closes. Repro steps and logs below.

alex: Can you paste the gateway logs and the exact client request? is the client using HTTP/2 to us or is the gateway doing h2->h1 translation?

samir: They provided this minimal curl they run through the gateway: 
```
curl -v -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-x\"
```
Gateway is translating h2 -> h1. Customer says gateway is a gRPC-web bridge (grpc-bridge v2.4).

jen: Common failure mode: intermediaries buffer until a threshold or until response end. SSE relies on flushes; if the gateway buffers and re-chunks, clients can get merged/partial events or an abrupt close. Any `transfer-encoding` or `content-length` anomalies in logs?

samir: On our side the runtime logs show we flushed three SSE payloads spaced ~700ms apart. Response headers we emitted: `HTTP/2 200`, `transfer-encoding: chunked`, `content-type: text/event-stream`. Gateway logs show: 
```
[gw] recv h2 frames len=1200
[gw] buffering: 809 bytes (threshold=8192)
[gw] flush -> sent 512 bytes to client
[gw] client closed connection after 12s
```
Client only received the first flush contents.

mike: Sounds like the gateway is re-chunking and/or truncating trailing flushes. Some gateways strip `Transfer-Encoding` or mishandle trailers. Do we have a wire capture from the gateway->client?

samir: They attached a tcpdump snippet showing the gateway sending a `RST` to client after sending a final HTTP/1.1 FIN. No trailer frames forwarded.

tara: Two quick workarounds to propose to customer: 1) disable proxy buffering (nginx: `proxy_buffering off` / `X-Accel-Buffering: no`) or 2) use websocket passthrough instead of SSE if gateway does not support unbuffered chunked responses. Have them also bump idle timeouts/keepalive.

alex: They tried `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the gateway but reported no change — gateway still internally buffers to 8k and re-chunks. If the bridge enforces a min-chunk size, small frequent flushes from us will be merged and then might be closed by a timeout.

jen: We should also check if the gateway converts HTTP/2 data frames into HTTP/1 chunked with different boundaries; re-chunking can combine multiple SSE events, causing the client SSE parser to see partial events if the gateway cuts mid-event. Also, idle timeout shorter than their event cadence will cause closure.

mike: Actionable triage items: can eng-runtime produce a test image that intentionally emits 3 SSE chunk sizes: small (200B), medium (2k), small (400B) with delays, then we run it behind a local grpc-bridge v2.4 to reproduce? If we can reproduce locally, we can test changing our flush behavior or adding `Connection: keep-alive` pings.

samir: Customer asked if we can change server behavior. Our runtime can adjust flush frequency (send slightly larger chunks less often) or insert keepalive comments (`:keepalive\n\n`) to keep intermediaries from timing out. Downsides: larger chunks can increase latency for early tokens; keepalives add bytes but are low cost.

tara: Also check for `Expect: 100-continue` oddities and whether the gateway is stripping `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header; if header removed, many proxies will buffer until full response.

alex: Recommend support message to customer: 1) try websocket fallback, 2) increase gateway idle timeout and disable internal buffering, 3) if possible, upgrade grpc-bridge to a version that preserves flush semantics, or 4) run the request directly to our h2 endpoint (skip the bridge). Provide them a docker-compose repro to test.

samir: Pasted repro snippet for customer / eng: 
```
# runtime container emits SSE every 700ms
while true; do printf '\\\\n:keepalive\\\\n'; sleep 0.7; printf 'data: {\"token\":\"%s\"}\n\\\\n' "$(head -c 6 /dev/urandom | base64)"; done
```
They can run this behind grpc-bridge to see buffering behavior.

mike: I'll try to reproduce with our grpc-bridge docker image and nghttpx/Envoy shim. If reproduced, we can open a runtime change request to try: a) configure a periodic keepalive comment, b) optionally coalesce flushes to meet common 8k thresholds, c) document websockets as fallback.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-9873 — eng-runtime / eng-infra to triage.

samir: Recording customer-facing steps to send now. Keeping thread open. cc @eng-runtime @eng-infra for repro and triage. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
